steps.title: Prepare surgical workspace
steps.instruction: Set up the surgical area and materials before starting the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Thaw Corning Matrigel Basement Membrane Matrix on ice (preferably at 4 °C) for 2–3 h prior to starting.
Refill the isoflurane tank to the maximum level to ensure sufficient supply for the entire procedure.
Apply opaque eye ointment to the mouse to prevent corneal drying and block bright light during anesthesia.
Turn on heating pads, set them to 37 °C, and place a piece of tissue between the mouse and the pad; keep pads on for the whole procedure.

steps.title: Set up endoscopy system
steps.instruction: Assemble and verify the adapted Image 1 Hub endoscope system before animal work.

substeps.instruction: Carefully twist off and remove the plastic cover of the telescope.
Remove the camera head lens cap by turning the black dial 90° clockwise and pulling the cap off while holding the dial at 90°.
Optional: Clean the telescope camera port and the camera head lens with Kimtech Science Delicate Task Wipers for optimal image quality.
Turn the black dial 90° clockwise again to align the telescope light port with the camera buttons; release the dial to lock the telescope in place.
Release the security lever 90° and gently pull the obturator out of the examination sheath.
Attach the obturator to the telescope and refasten the security lever, aligning it with the indentation on the sheath.
Screw the light source onto the telescope light port.
Screw the air pump onto the air valve of the examination sheath and close the extra air valve (lever perpendicular to the inlet tube).
Confirm that the camera and endoscope are fully assembled as shown in Figure 3 (without the injection needle).
Turn on the Image 1 HUB endoscopy system, the light source, and the air pump.
Test airflow by placing the endoscope tip inside a 15 mL Falcon tube filled with PBS (1X) at room temperature; adjust the air‑valve lever to obtain 1 bubble per second.
Select the white‑balance setting in the camera menu, pointing the endoscope at a white surface, and proceed only after successful balance.
Insert a USB device into the HUB to record images and/or videos.

steps.title: Prepare organoid injection suspension
steps.instruction: Process mouse intestinal organoids and formulate the injection mixture.

substeps.instruction: Wash organoid domes once with 500 µL of PBS (1X) at room temperature.
Overlay the domes with 350 µL of Corning Cell Recovery Solution and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Mechanically dissociate organoids into fragments of ~10–20 cells each using a pre‑wet P20 tip stacked on a P1000 tip (chemical dissociation with TrypLE Express may be needed for some lines).
Collect the fragment suspension in a Falcon tube and centrifuge at 350 g for 5 min; resuspend the pellet in the injection solution (PBS 1X + 10 % Matrigel + 10 µM Y‑27632).

Inject ~150 fragments (≈10–20 cells per fragment) per injection using 100 µL of the suspension; perform up to three injections per mouse as needed (e.g., ~three 50 µL Matrigel domes for APKS or MT577 T1‑2 organoids). Adjust fragment number and injection count based on mutational profile and growth potential.
Store the organoid fragments in the injection solution on ice and proceed to orthotopic injection within 3 h to maintain viability.
